_about: The journey, one record per milestone, read by milestones.py to write the timeline into the showcase (for Anthropic) and the pitch (for funders). Facts are shared; each audience has its own words. 'status' is done | running | waiting | proposed. 'today' marks where the past ends. Keep internal detail (reporters' names, the report list's access problems) out of this file: both pages are read outside the team. 'team' lists the internal pages and source projects behind each milestone, for the team map only.

anthropic.line: For years, what the digital age gave a tradition was a picture of its book. The words were there; the chant, the commentary beside the verse and the teacher's voice were not.

funder.title: The book, scanned
funder.line: A scan holds the words of a book. It cannot hold the chant, the commentary beside the verse, or the teacher's voice. For most of the tradition's texts, that is where things stood.

pages: The showcase: the book, scanned, beside the chant

milestones.title: One person asks, Claude Code builds

number.label: prompts for each published piece of work, April to September

anthropic.line: The trustee asks, and Claude Code builds: the Jaiminīya Sāmaveda brought out of a proprietary font, then nine sites open to anyone. A pāṭhaśālā proofreads, and someone who lives near it learns the tools and takes the work over.

funder.title: Nine sites, open to anyone

number.label: verses in the one index every site checks against

funder.line: The texts with their commentaries and their recitation, to read, search and listen to: the Veda with the text following the chant, 8,391 Purāṇa verses heard at the second a teacher chants them, Śaṅkara's commentaries with Tamil and English beside them.
funder.software: builds the sites and keeps them linked

pages: The showcase: seven moments from the sessions
The showcase: the Jaiminīya Sāmaveda handed over

milestones.title: Claude Code checks its own work

number.label: flags where the two editions' reading was exactly the editor's own fix

anthropic.line: One request, then a check that runs on everything. Every Mahābhārata verse is compared with two other editions, and every page of the Yajurveda commentary is read against the printed book. Only the differences go to a person, laid out beside the evidence.
anthropic.claude: reads, compares, measures itself on mistakes already known
anthropic.decides: reviewers, and a vidvān against the printed page

funder.title: Every verse checked against a second witness

number.label: printed pages of the Yajurveda commentary read against its typed text

funder.line: The typed Mahābhārata is compared verse by verse with two other editions, and the Yajurveda commentary page by page with the printed book. A reviewer or a vidvān sees only where they differ, with the evidence laid out beside it.
funder.software: reads, compares, sets aside what agrees
funder.decides: reviewers, and a vidvān against the printed page

Correction loop, case 2: against two editions

milestones.title: A whole book in thirteen days

number.label: scanned pages, from the scans to a searchable edition linked with Kane

anthropic.line: The Smṛtimuktāphalam, a digest of dharma in a Tamil edition. Claude Code found the scan's own faults (leaves upside down, out of order, scanned twice, missing), checked the book's contents list against its body, and traced 407 of Kane's footnotes to their source.
anthropic.decides: the team; a vidvān's reading of the text is still to come

funder.title: A 4,333-page digest, searchable in thirteen days

number.label: of Kane's footnotes traced to the verse they quote

funder.line: The Smṛtimuktāphalam, Vaidyanātha Dīkṣita's digest of dharma, from scans to a searchable edition: every section and quotation indexed, and linked both ways with Kane's History of Dharmaśāstra. An out-of-print commentary would be published the same way.
funder.software: reads the scans, finds their faults, builds the edition
funder.decides: the team; a vidvān's reading of the text is still to come

number.label: of the readers' open reports on verses were already flagged by the check, before anyone opened them

anthropic.line: A report button on the Mahābhārata site: select a word, tap. 820 reports in three weeks, most from one proofreader working parva by parva. And when a reader said a link did nothing on their phone, one screenshot from that phone settled a fault no test could reproduce.

funder.title: Readers find the mistakes

number.label: reports from readers of the Mahābhārata in three weeks

funder.line: A reader selects a word that looks wrong and taps. Most reports come from one proofreader, working parva by parva. More than half of them already have the other editions' reading waiting for the reviewer.

pages: Fix loop: "I click a link and nothing happens"

milestones.title: The report button starts the loops

anthropic.line: Each report says what kind it is: a typing mistake, a name to explain, a page that is not working, an idea. An agent does the first check for that kind and puts it in front of the right person. When the fix lands, the agent closes the report and tells the reader.
anthropic.starts: any reader, or a vidvān with a private link

funder.title: Every report reaches the right person
funder.line: Each report says what kind it is: a typing mistake, a name to explain, a page that is not working, an idea. It goes to the person who can decide it, with the first check already done, and the reader hears back when it is fixed.

pages: The report button: routing reports to the loops

milestones.title: Agents run the loops; students and vidvāns rule

number.label: verses of the Harivaṃśa in the first index of names, half with agents and half without

anthropic.line: A pāṭhaśālā student is asked, "Do you have a character you like?" Agents find the verses, hand them out, chase, compare and rebuild the site. Students read each verse; a vidvān signs. The pilot measures one thing above all: minutes of people's time for each signed verse.
anthropic.claude: every step between the question and the signature

funder.title: The first index of names for a Purāṇa

number.label: for the Harivaṃśa pilot: 16,100 verses, up to 4,034 names, nine months

funder.line: Pāṭhaśālā students read each verse that names a person, and a vidvān signs every entry. Half the chapters are done with software doing the legwork and half without, so the time it saves is measured, not claimed.
funder.software: finds the verses, hands them out, keeps the work moving
